title: StructuredGradeRecord
description: The GRADE verdict as structured output rather than prose. Today GRADE is model-authored prose that pipeline_sot.py:43 regex-scrapes with a permissive 'Not Determined' default; this record replaces that with a fail-closed contract. Produced by Claude (the GRADE verdict is Claude's under the allocation table), validated by Python. It is the input the 確信度 lookup needs, what makes the step-8 bias rollup countable, and the ONLY source of net_direction — the step pack must never feed the posterior, because it is a presentation projection where one finding referenced by three steps would be weighted three times.

level.description: Certainty of the body of evidence.

downgrades.description: At most ONE entry per domain — aggregate before writing. Uniqueness is enforced in Python (JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness by property): without it sum(downgrades[].steps) double-counts and net_direction is wrong, which is why 'deduplicated by construction' was an unearned claim.

upgrades.description: At most ONE entry per domain, same reason.

steps.description: GRADE rates down or up by one level (serious) or two (very serious). Anything else is a data error.

evidence.description: Why this modifier applies. A quoted locator when the reason is stated in a paper; a derived record when it is computed from the data — an imprecision downgrade read off a confidence interval exists in no paper as text.
